parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer with a comparatively restrained state. Universal exposures: the 2025 sex-binary order and Nov-2025 Supreme Court ruling eliminate X/new mismatched markers (X valid only to expiry), a Feb-2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, eight-plus governments issued travel advisories, and trans travelers report confiscated/blocking passports and stranding. The federal order also bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities nationwide, including here. Federal custody carries conversion-therapy-style policies and documented immigration-custody abuse. The state offsets locally: July-2026 'low-risk' grouping, gubernatorial vetoes of bathroom bills, employment/public-accommodation protections, no documented trans-directed arrest or violence here. No imprisonment for being trans is documented; entry refusal, humiliation and facility exclusion dominate.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb-2025 end of X/mismatched markers; Nov-2025 court lets restrictions take effect; cable orders refusal on sex discrepancy with possible lifetime fraud finding; trans travelers report passports confiscated/blocked and stranding; 8+ foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, with limited waiver; ACLU suit pending in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Border refusal feeds state-level experience: a denied or flagged traveller never reaches the state's protections; litigation may change rules mid-travel.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for transgender inmates from 2026 (hair cut, hormones removed); transgender men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009; state records no trans-directed arrest or detention here (absence not proof of safety).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any state-level stop that escalates to federal or immigration custody imports the documented federal custody harm; state restraint does not bind federal actors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Jan-2025 executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities nationwide — a universal exposure reaching this state; nationally 9+1 units ban gender-congruent facility use in all government buildings, 4 states criminalise in some circumstances with one 2025 arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state's governor vetoed bathroom and pronoun bills in June 2023; it sits in the July-2026 low-risk group and is not listed among banning states; municipal ordinances in nine cities cover public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules operate inside the state regardless of local vetoes; local protective ordinances carry religious/governmental/small-business exemptions.

care_services.exposure: 1982 Medicaid surgery exclusion unresolved against a 2020 challenge and a 2023 order; visitor-facing emergency-care refusal on trans status is not documented either way; federal subpoenas of under-19 patient records signal surveillance of care seekers.
care_services.protection: June-2023 executive order extends gender-affirming coverage to state employees over 21; conversion therapy barred from government funding; county-level ban since 2017.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor's care needs fall under federal youth-care hostility (EO calling care 'mutilation', funding bans), which state orders cannot override for federal programmes.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy (May-2026) prioritises groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; advocates compare trajectory to early genocide stages; 66% public support for birth-sex markers; Pride organisation in the state's second city dissolved Jan-2026.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Federal documents state counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; the reward is not conditioned on the phrase; state leadership has actively vetoed anti-trans bills.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National framing raises street-level and official friction even where state officials are protective; Pride collapse signals narrowing civic space locally.

minors_guardians.exposure: EOs direct law enforcement to investigate schools and criminally prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; youth care banned in 27 states nationally; this state bars transition surgery on minors and trans girls from female sports; travel-guide advisories from allied governments target trans travellers generally.
minors_guardians.protection: July-2026 assessment judges the state's youth policies unlikely to extend to adults; state vetoes protected school safe spaces; no documented enforcement against a visiting family.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling trans adult with a gender-diverse minor faces both the federal document/entry regime and state youth restrictions if any service or school contact occurs during the stay.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Gay-and-trans panic defence remains available at common law with reform bills lapsing; state hate-crime statute omits gender identity; only 23 states nationally cover it; Pride cancellation suggests deteriorating visible presence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment and public-accommodation protections operate via Title VII, a 2023 executive order and nine municipal ordinances; the well-documented dossier records no trans-directed violence here.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Panic defence interacts with any assault case, weakening recourse even where national hate-crime charges are theoretically available.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Multiple federal orders blocked or enjoined yet in flux — exposure depends on which measures are operative on travel dates; Medicaid-exclusion conflict, birth-certificate litigation status and low-risk criteria are unresolved; police responses to trans visitors undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have enjoined several orders; legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules; state-level vetoes and DOJ affirmations show institutions working for trans people at this level.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Active litigation makes outcomes date-sensitive: a traveller could arrive under a restraining order or a newly effective restriction.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than ours: Vellandra denies admission categorically through an unpublished register with near-zero appeal. Here entry refusal is conditional on document discrepancy, the fraud finding is non-automatic with waiver, and the restriction is actively litigated; in-state the person is not excluded from all services.

Similar entry mechanics (secondary screening, discretionary refusal, administrative not criminal outcomes, slow remedies). Ours sits below because it adds a federal facility-exclusion order, documented federal custody abuse, conversion-therapy-style prison policy and official threat-framing absent from Kestrel Isles.

Higher than ours: trained officers, appeals tribunal, compensation for detention, respectful inspection. Here the operative cable instructs refusal on sex doubt, trans travellers report stranded passports, and multiple governments warn their citizens — the border layer works against trans travellers, not for them.

Closest match: routine document/record exposure with verification detentions, inconsistent enforcement, thin legal aid, and uncertainty about when checks become punishment. Ours has stronger local protections and no documented state arrest, but a more explicitly adverse national document regime.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences one system: federal document, border, facility and custody rules run through this state, while the state layer is genuinely protective but limited in reach. The entry-document regime is the heaviest, near-universal exposure — markers fixed to assigned sex, refusal instructions on discrepancy, documented stranding and foreign advisories — meaning discovery at the border can end the trip before local protections matter. In-state, federal facility exclusion in government-funded buildings plus official anti-trans framing create continuous low-grade exposure, while gubernatorial vetoes, municipal ordinances, employment protections, a national hate-crime statute and a well-documented absence of trans-directed violence here pull the score up. Custody exposures (federal immigration and corrections practices) are severe but conditional. Net: elevated, non-criminal, institutionally contested risk — roughly the 0.45–0.50 band.
